messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: arguments imply differing number of rows
parts:
fit3 <- lavaan(model = third_model, data = d,
               model.type = "sem", meanstructure = "default",
               int.ov.free = FALSE, int.lv.free = FALSE, fixed.x = F,
               orthogonal = FALSE, std.lv = FALSE,
               parameterization = "default", auto.fix.first = F,
               auto.fix.single = T, auto.var = T, auto.cov.lv.x = FALSE,
               auto.cov.y = T, auto.th = T, auto.delta = FALSE,
               std.ov = FALSE, missing = "default",
               constraints = "", estimator = "ML",
               zero.cell.warn = TRUE, start = "default")

Most of these settings are the defaults for the sem() function, so it might be easier to just use that.  The only thing you set differently is a setting that doesn't matter (auto.cov.lv.x = FALSE doesn't apply to your model because you have no exogenous latent variables, and auto.th = TRUE doesn't apply because you have continuous indicators) and a specification that doesn't make any sense: auto.fix.single = TRUE means you fix the residual variances of single-indicators to zero, but you have specified nonzero values in your syntax. 

When I import your data and run this, I get no error:

fit3 <- sem(third_model, data = d, fixed.x = FALSE)
summary(fit3, modindices = TRUE)


Terry
